collection: NERDC JSS 1 Cultural and Creative Arts dance and choreography
note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise how deliberate movement and timing can communicate an idea.
questions.prompt: A group wants to show the idea of waiting for rain through dance. Which plan most clearly uses movement to express the idea?
questions.answer: Arrange slow reaching movements, a timed pause and a quicker response when the imagined rain begins.
questions.explanation: The ordered movements and changes in timing communicate expectation and response through the body.
options: Read a weather notice while everyone sits still.
Arrange slow reaching movements, a timed pause and a quicker response when the imagined rain begins.
Display a picture of clouds beside an empty stage.
List the names of places with heavy rainfall.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a documented Nigerian traditional dance and distinguish its name from that of an instrument.
questions.prompt: A display has separate labels for Nigerian dance traditions and musical instruments. Which label belongs in the dance section?
questions.explanation: Atilogwu is documented as a dance. The other choices name musical instruments.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Perform a basic teacher-demonstrated phrase from an identified Nigerian dance tradition.
questions.prompt: Your teacher will name and demonstrate a basic phrase from a Nigerian traditional dance. Watch the feet and listen for the pulse. After one rehearsal, perform the phrase twice and finish on the demonstrated cue.
questions.answer: A successful performance reproduces the demonstrated sequence and weight changes at the agreed pace. It keeps the pulse through both repetitions and stops at the cue.
questions.explanation: The teacher’s chosen demonstration supplies the reference. Classroom scoring uses the demonstrated phrase and a manageable pace.

markingGuide.description: Performs the demonstrated steps in order.
Shows the demonstrated weight changes or an agreed equivalent.
Keeps a recognisable pulse across both repetitions.

questions.administrationNote: Use a documented basic phrase appropriate to the class and record the dance name, source and agreed adaptation. Demonstrate the phrase and cue before assessment. Use a clear floor and a comfortable pace.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify choreography as the deliberate arrangement of movements for a performance.
questions.prompt: Which decision by a dance group is an example of choreography?
questions.answer: Arrange a turn after the first phrase and set the count for everyone to enter together.
questions.explanation: Arranging when and how dancers move is choreography. The other activities support the event without arranging movement.
options: Arrange a turn after the first phrase and set the count for everyone to enter together.
Decide where to store the costumes after the show.
Choose the order in which tickets are collected.
Make a list of people who attended the rehearsal.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how repetition and contrast help an audience recognise changes in a movement phrase.
questions.prompt: A group uses the sequence reach, close, reach, close. On the final repetition it changes the last close to a wide stretch. Explain what stays recognisable and how the changed ending can draw attention.
questions.answer: The repeated reach-and-close actions establish a pattern. The final wide stretch breaks that pattern, so the last moment can stand out.
questions.explanation: Repetition lets the audience form an expectation. Contrast directs attention to a departure from it.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the movement idea that repeats.
Explains the likely effect on the audience.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Create and perform a short movement phrase that changes level and repeats a motif.
questions.prompt: Create and perform an eight-count movement phrase in your own space. Repeat one small movement idea and change level once. Use a standing or seated level change that you can control.
questions.answer: For example, reach and return on counts one and two, repeat on three and four, lower the reach on five and six, and settle on seven and eight.
questions.explanation: A recognisable repeated action makes a motif. Changing the reach level adds a clear variation without requiring travel.

markingGuide.description: Performs a phrase with a clear eight-count structure.
Shows a controlled change of level.
Ends with a clear finish on the agreed count.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Arrange and perform a partner sequence with a staggered entry and a shared finish.
questions.prompt: With a partner, design a two-count gesture that the second dancer begins two counts after the first. Both should finish with the same pose on count six. Perform the sequence without crossing paths.
questions.answer: The first dancer performs the gesture on counts one and two, then holds. The second performs the same gesture on counts three and four. Both prepare on count five and reach the same pose on six.
questions.explanation: Staggering the same movement creates a simple canon. The shared finishing count brings the pair together.

markingGuide.description: Uses the same recognisable gesture for both dancers.
Staggers the second entry by two counts.
Reaches the shared pose together on count six.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Create and perform a clear formation change using an agreed cue.
questions.prompt: In a group of four, begin in a spaced line and finish in two spaced pairs. Plan a cue to start the transition and use a comfortable walking pace. Each pupil should show where they will finish before the group performs.
questions.answer: One option is to split the line into adjacent pairs. At the leader’s raised hand, the front pair stays in place and turns inward while the second pair walks a short distance to an agreed mark. Both pairs arrive facing the audience at the end.
questions.explanation: A shared cue and agreed destinations make the formation change clear. Each pupil can plan a route that leaves space for the others.

markingGuide.description: Begins with a recognisable line and ends in two pairs.
Moves to the agreed destination at a controlled pace.
Maintains clear spacing and finishes with the group.
